stem: A client demonstrates a home peritoneal-dialysis exchange. Which action indicates a need for further teaching?

options.A: Performing hand hygiene before handling the dialysis connection
options.B: Avoiding contact with the open ends of the transfer set and dialysis line
options.C: Contacting the dialysis team promptly if the exchange connection becomes contaminated
options.D: Touching the open transfer-set connection because the hands were cleaned immediately beforehand

rationale: ISPD guidance treats breach of aseptic technique or touch contamination of the connection during a PD exchange as contamination that can increase peritonitis risk and advises patients to seek prompt guidance from the dialysis team when sterility is breached. Hand hygiene and adherence to aseptic exchange technique are emphasized in PD training. Therefore D requires correction: clean hands do not make touching an open connection an acceptable technique. A and B reduce contamination risk, and C is the recommended response when exchange sterility is breached.
educational_objective: Use hand hygiene and aseptic non-touch principles during peritoneal-dialysis exchanges and recognize touch contamination of an open connection as a safety breach requiring prompt dialysis-team guidance.
source_document_title: ISPD peritonitis guideline recommendations: 2022 update on prevention and treatment
source_version_date: 2022 guideline; 2023 and 2024 corrigenda reviewed; current ISPD guideline listing accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Prevention of peritonitis > Contamination of PD system: patients should immediately seek advice if sterility of a PD exchange is breached; wet contamination examples include breach of aseptic technique or touch contamination of the connection during an exchange. Training programme: deviations from appropriate hand-hygiene protocols or aseptic technique are identified as exchange-technique problems requiring reassessment/retraining.
source_claim_supported: PD exchanges require contamination-prevention practices including hand hygiene and aseptic handling of connections; touching an open connection is a sterility breach and should prompt dialysis-team advice.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Printed page 14, Physiological Adaptation: perform and manage care of a client receiving peritoneal dialysis; recognize signs/situations of complications and intervene.
blueprint_topic: Physiological Adaptation — safe peritoneal-dialysis exchange technique and contamination prevention
correction_summary: Removed the overbroad 'strict sterile technique throughout' statement and rebuilt the item around ISPD-supported hand hygiene, aseptic non-touch handling and contamination response. Corrected blueprint from Basic Care and Comfort to Physiological Adaptation.
audit_findings: ISPD directly supports touch contamination as a breach and prompt contact with the dialysis team, while training guidance emphasizes hand hygiene/aseptic technique. D is the only unsafe action; A-C are appropriate. No glove, mask, antibiotic, or universal sterile-field rule is asserted beyond source support. Blueprint is an exact NCSBN 2026 PD-management match. Independent adversarial second pass found no second answer, cueing, ambiguity or unresolved conflict.
